Ahh lucky hoping you find a way to review this!!!

So, a Russian-owned hospitality project affordable for typical Russian vacationers

Glad that you identified correctly that the brands are licensing their names. Agree with the comment about unique ports and places. These cruises seem to go to the usual places.

I think it's time to call "yacht top". I can't see how there's a big enough market for this experience at the price point the high end brands are all trying to compete at. It was a great first mover idea but just so easily replicated with zero real differentiation between the products. It's not like a physical location - anyone can come dock and get high end passengers from the port you want to operate from. I can see this becoming an economic bloodbath. It's not like these are low cost to operate and you can send a cruise out half empty and it work out okay. Maintenance, fuel, crew levels - it's all playing the game on hard mode. Will be very interesting to see how this shakes out. Would love to know the occupancy assumptions for the economics to work.

Wow, I wasn't expecting Aman to attempt to position themselves even higher than Orient (with overlap). At the current trajectory, we only need a handful of more hotel chains to jump in before we get a cruising yacht that's literally just a mega yacht for one customer :D Very interesting how this is all shaking out though. Ritz-Carlton really isn't even in the same category. Starting at $1K-$1.5K a night, they really aren't competitors with the others. Four Seasons is starting to seem like the "budget" ultra-luxury cruise line. Starts at $3K-$5K per night, but includes barely anything. The Spirit Airlines of the ultra-luxury crowd, if you will. You can "save" money for an Instagram worthy cruise, but only if you pack a load of granola bars. Also, service apparently leaves a lot to be desired. Orient starts at $4K-$6K per night, so there's overlap with Four Seasons. Starts to look like the actual better value when you look at what's included. Aman starts at $6K-$8K, so no real overlap with Four Seasons, and it butts up against the Orient. However, the real cost is quite a bit higher due to lack of inclusions. The Orient Express has an amazing looking yacht, so Aman really has no room for error if they want to convince people to pay more for theirs. I'm with you, Ben, in that this whole situation is fascinating to me in a way that I can't really explain. Will be entertaining to see who succeeds and who fails.

#6265. The Very Best Thai Food in New York City

There are several ways to describe delicious food in Thai: Aroy means delicious, while aroy mak takes it a step further to very delicious. But my favorite word is zaab (also spelled zabb or zab; แซ่บ), a term rooted in the Isan region of northeastern Thailand that conveys a bold deliciousness, often associated with the heat. In New York City, we’re spoiled for choice when it comes to food that delivers true zaab.

I’ve spent my life immersed in the world of Thai food. One of the joys of growing up in a Thai restaurant family is participating in one of our favorite hobbies: scoping out other Thai restaurants to see what’s good. Most summers, my aunts would close down their restaurant in Royal Palm Beach for two weeks, and they’d road trip from South Florida up to New York City to check out casinos and taste Thai restaurants along the way—when I was lucky, I got to join them. My grandpa, for his part, used to drive to the city weekly to get products for his grocery store in Washington, DC, and through his firsthand research, old friends, and the Internet, he created detailed restaurant guides to help me find footing when I moved to the city almost five years ago.

As I continue to eat my way through the city’s Thai restaurants, I feel spoiled for choice. More and more chefs are serving regional specialties of their hometowns and maintaining Thai food’s great balancing act between the spice, acid, salt, sweetness, and umami, while incorporating their own signature flair.

While the city’s established Thai spots, particularly out in Elmhurst, Queens, remain beloved, plenty of the most compelling and exciting bites can be found in various parts of the city. There has never been a more exciting time to eat Thai food in NYC, and these 14 restaurants best embody its golden era.

If you want an overview of the best dishes across Thailand without leaving the city, let your first stop in Queen’s Little Thai Town be Ayada. The beloved restaurant has familiar favorites like pad thai and tom yum, but let its expertise in other regional favorites be an excuse to try my dad’s favorite Yen Ta Fo, a bubblegum-pink soup with soft rice noodles and a savory tomato and bean curd sauce.

364 Grand Street, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg)

Must-order dish: Any of the fiery curries on the rotating menu

When the news of Ugly Baby’s closure last year hit my WhatsApp chat with my Thai friends, you would’ve thought that someone had died. In a way, it felt like we lost a family member. Ugly Baby was one of the rare spots in the city that didn’t hold back on heat like many in America do to appease Western palates and milder heat tolerances. But all was saved when the beloved restaurant announced its reopening in Williamsburg earlier this fall. It’s now a fun, lively two-floor restaurant with eclectic dishware and recipes from various Thai provinces, including brutally hot curries from Southern Thailand and Northeastern Isan cuisine.

Its menu is sorted from least spicy to most spicy—written out as “the laughs” to “the ugly” (dishes toward the latter end consist of a few menu items that will make you feel like you’re breathing fire). Luckily, waiters are standing by with large jugs of water, ready to refill at the sight of sweat dripping down your forehead.

Bangkok Supper Club makes a convincing case for the arrival of upscale Thai dining.

Order a la carte, or do the $150 tasting menu at Bangkok Supper Club.

641 Hudson St, New York, NY 10014 (Meatpacking District)

With an award-winning cocktail program by Suwincha "Chacha" Singsuwan and a menu from executive chef Max Wittawat, Bangkok Supper Club makes a convincing case for the arrival of upscale Thai dining. The drinks are as much of a draw as the food. I like to start my meal with a fish sauce cocktail, a savory, umami-forward drink that captures the depth of fish sauce while balancing it with sweet notes of floral pear. It’s unexpected, but feels just right, and is a lovely accompaniment to my other must-order: the pork jowl. These deep-fried pork cheeks arrive atop a fragrant, garlic-baked rice.

One of the best parts about eating in Thailand is getting food from restaurants and stalls that specialize in one singular dish. As my dad says, that’s how you know it’s good. Eim Khao Mun Kai is one such place. Its one dish, khao mun gai, is the Thai version of Hainanese chicken rice, served with a spicy, fermented bean sauce.

The $12 set meal includes tender steamed chicken thighs made with halal meat and gizzards, fragrant ginger rice that’s cooked with chicken droppings, and a savory broth-based soup made from the bones, with sides of cilantro and cucumber plus plenty of sauce. It’s a tight shop and cash-only. When my dad comes into town, it’s the first place we go to.

Must-order dish: Northern-style curry noodles

Since 1990, this institution has been serving what my friend calls “old-school auntie energy” with wooden accents, white tablecloths, and a sprawling menu. When I say sprawling, I mean it. You can flip through pages at SriPraPhai and can eat all the fried meats, papaya salads, curries, and noodle dishes your heart desires.

Zaab Zaab specializes in Northeast Isan cuisine, repping where both owners are from.

76-04 Woodside Ave, Queens, NY 11373 (Elmhurst)

208 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg)

Zaab Zaab has locations in both Elmhurst and Williamsburg, and specializes in Northeast Isan cuisine from where owner Bryan Chunton and chef Aniwat Khotsopa hail. The restaurant’s signature dish, an herb-packed larb ped udon, features cilantro- and mint-packed ground duck, fried liver, and crispy skin; it’s served with a plethora of fresh lettuce, cabbage, extra herbs, and sticky rice. When I go with a group, though, I also make sure we order the pla neung manow, which comes steamed with a chili, garlic, and lime sauce that’s so flavorful, you’ll want to drink it like soup (luckily it’s served with little bowls so you can).

800 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg)

Must-order dish: Chor muang for an appetizer; pad kea mao seafood as a main

Focusing on 19th- century recipes from the royal consort court, Kaew Jao Jorm’s (named after the former King Rama V’s favorite flower) serves a regal menu in its intimate, 20-seat restaurant. The exterior is on an unassuming street in Williamsburg, but inside, it is the restaurant incarnation of Mary Poppins' bag: compact, but they manage to pack in far more than you’d expect.

Though the signature dumplings, chor muang—chicken and peanut filling encased in delicate butterfly pea flower dough—are the star, don’t overlook the noodle dishes, which are slurpable, expertly sauced, and so soft as to be almost buttery.

Thai Diner does diner favorites reimagined, like their beloved Thai Disco Fries.

Head to Thai Diner for brunch, lunch, or a vibey dinner.

If you have friends from out of town that you really want to impress and show how fun eating in New York City can be, go to Thai Diner and get an order of the Thai Disco Fries. I find that these crispy, crinkle-cut fries smothered in a peanutty massaman curry sauce are delicious enough to justify to out-of-towners how much you overspend on rent. Reservations can be hard to get, but they do take some walk-ins, so your best bet is to either arrive slightly before opening, or put your name down and wander around Nolita until your name is called.

The restaurant has a tropical dive bar feel, with plenty of diner favorites reimagined like a custardy Thai tea babka, French toast, and a signature Thai Diner egg sandwich made with Isan-style sausage wrapped in a plush roti. Co-owners Ann Redding and Matt Danzer also recently opened Mommy Pai’s, a fast Thai chicken takeout spot on the same block that’s a great lunch spot without the wait.

Dishes are meant to be shared family-style here—like a whole fish drenched in cliantro-lime broth.

661 Driggs Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Williamsburg)

Must-order dish: Steamed fish with Thai herbs

Specializing in seafood dishes, Fish Cheeks focuses on the bright flavors of southern coastal Thailand. Dishes are meant to be shared family-style here, and though the menu features a few poultry, pork, and beef options, your best bet is trusting the name and going straight for fish. I recommend getting a whole steamed fish for the table—your dinnermates will relish in sharing the communal centerpiece and drenching rice in its cilantro-lime broth, or the coconut crab curry, which comes with rice noodles for soaking up every last bit of the creamy sauce.

Though its flagship Noho location can book out quickly, its equally delicious (and newer) spot in Williamsburg is a bit easier to secure a reservation at, for now.

New Flatiron restaurant LenLen is definitively cool.

The menu at LenLen includes crowd-pleasers and bolder dishes like a durian crab curry.

40 E 20th St, New York, NY 10003 (Flatiron)

If I had to describe LenLen in one word, it would be cool. This relatively new spot hit Flatiron earlier this year, bringing a fresh excitement to the Thai food scene in midtown. For me, the standout of the menu is the love-it-or-loathe-it durian crab curry. It’s earthy, fruity, and well worth the visit alone. While you’re there, order the wagyu beef boat noodles, too, which are served in a rich, dark broth that reminds me of the ones I’ve had in Ayutthaya, one of my favorite cities in Thailand (and the birthplace of boat noodles).

There are whispers of a speakeasy opening downstairs in the coming months, which gives the restaurant extra potential to become a go-to dinner spot that seamlessly transitions into a night out.

Ler Lers does classic Bangkok-style fare right.

From pad thai to grilled meats, Ler Lers does it all.

417 Tompkins Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11216 (Bed-Stuy)

Not to be confused with LenLen, Ler Lers is a newer spot in Bed-Stuy and does classic Bangkok-style fare right. Its ambiance is stylish and warm, with a mix of rattan and earthy tones, for a setting that makes sipping on a sweet iced Thai tea feel right even on a cold rainy day.

I’m pretty weary of ordering pad thai out in restaurants, just because the cuisine has so much else to offer. But a friend promised me that the pad thai topped with crispy pork belly was “awesome,” and after trying it for myself, I’ve started saying the same to friends and family. The rest of the menu has a lot of other familiar favorites like fried rice and grilled meats, and if you’re someone who enjoys a sticky tamarind sauce as much as I do, try the branzino, too.

Hommali is stylish in every sense of the word, from the plating to the space.

The Hommali cocktail menu is also expansive—go for the signature tomato option.

28 7th Ave S, New York, NY 10014 (West Village)

A newcomer to the West Village restaurant scene, this design-forward space has some serious pedigree with a menu curated by Bangkok-native Chattchakorn “Benz” Khajornchaisan, formerly of Eleven Madison Park. The restaurant is stylish in every sense of the word, with sage green tiles, oak accents, and warm lighting.

You can’t customize spice level here, so expect to get a little red from dishes like the prik larb beef tartare that comes with crispy tripe chips and is fiery with northern larb spices. The Hommali Five Spice dry-aged duck is also a standout and comes with fragrant rice that’s cooked in duck drippings. My opinion? The best order is getting the panang curry with tender beef cheek. It’s spicy, nutty, and you’ll want to order a side (or two) of roti to soak up that sauce.

The cocktail menu is also expansive—go for the signature tomato cocktail, which is vodka and rice wine-based with tomato extract, poblanos, and tamarind.

Soothr in the East Village specializes in noodles from all across Thailand.

204 E 13th St, New York, NY 10003 (East Village)

25-20 43rd Ave, Long Island City, NY 11101

Must-order dish: Sukhothai-style tom yum noodle soup

Thai noodle shop Soothr specializes in noodles from all across Thailand, and though the stir-fried variety is delicious, the soup noodles are the real standout. The Sukhothai-style tom yum noodle soup is a must-order, and encapsulates the best of Thai noodle soups with a deeply savory-acidic broth topped with bouncy fish cakes, meatballs, and rice noodles. Soothr has a new-ish Long Island City location that’s got a more nightlife vibe to it (and just as great noodles).

Kru in Williamsburg draws on Thailand’s vast culinary history, reimaging regional traditions through a contemporary lens.

90 N 14 St, Brooklyn, NY 11249 (Williamsburg)

Must-order dish: Lamb massaman curry pot pie

Named after the Thai word for “mentor,” chef Ohm Suansilphong honors the many teachers in his life through Kru. Here, he draws on Thailand’s vast culinary history, reimaging regional traditions through a contemporary lens. This looks like a crispy, massaman curry pot pie sprinkled with slow-cooked, pull-apart jackfruit, and tender lamb or tamarind-chili coated calamari that’s sweet, salty, and a little spicy. Chef adds and tweaks the menu seasonally, but I suggest the first thing you eat is always the Ma Hor, a savory bite of seasoned meat atop fresh fruit. The word means galloping horse, and it has enough warmth to open your tastebuds for the rest of the meal. Pay attention to the wine list: the restaurant is just as thoughtful about its award-winning program as it is the rest of the menu. Consider this a go-to as worthy of casual weeknight dinners as it is of special occasions.

As the most discerning, up-to-the-minute voice in all things travel, Condé Nast Traveler is the global citizen’s bible and muse, offering both inspiration and vital intel. We understand that time is the greatest luxury, which is why Condé Nast Traveler mines its network of experts and influencers so that you never waste a meal, a drink, or a hotel stay wherever you are in the world.

#6264. Southwest Performance Business Card Review: Is The $299 Annual Fee Worth It?

The Southwest® Rapid Rewards® Performance Business Credit Card is the most premium card in the Chase and Southwest co-brand card portfolio. This card currently has a $299 annual fee and comes with many helpful perks when you fly Southwest, including a free checked bag, complimentary upgrades to Preferred seating when available, and an anniversary bonus of 9,000 points every year.

If you frequently travel with Southwest and qualify for a small business credit card, this card is worth a closer look. That’s especially true now, because not only is it offering a welcome bonus of 80,000 bonus points, but now is also your last chance to earn a Southwest credit card welcome bonus that counts toward the Companion Pass. I’ll get into all of that and more below, as this is my in-depth Southwest Performance Business Card review.

Link: Learn more about the Southwest® Rapid Rewards® Performance Business Credit Card

Before I cover the Southwest Performance Business Card perks in detail, here’s a high-level view of this business credit card’s key details:

I also put together my pros and cons for the Southwest Performance Business Card:

When applying for a credit card, major considerations include the welcome bonus, the eligibility rules, and the fees, so let’s start by taking a look at those details for the Southwest Performance Business Card.

The Southwest Performance Business Card currently has a welcome bonus where you can earn 80,000 bonus points after spending $5,000 within the first three months.

Southwest Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider the points to be worth 1.2 cents each. That means I consider the 80,000 points to be worth $960, which is a solid bonus for a card like this (though admittedly we’ve seen slightly better limited time offers in the past).

When it comes to Southwest credit card eligibility rules, you’re potentially eligible for the Southwest Performance Business Card (including the welcome bonus) if you don’t currently have this card, and if you haven’t received a new cardmember bonus on this card in the past 24 months. You can have any of the Southwest personal cards, and/or the Southwest Premier Business Card, and they won’t impact eligibility for this card.

Beyond that, be aware of the general restrictions on applying for Chase cards. This includes the Chase 5/24 rule, whereby you generally won’t be approved for a Chase card if you’ve opened five or more cards in the last 24 months. That said, business credit cards aren’t always included on your credit report, so they often don’t count toward 5/24.

The Southwest Performance Business Card has a $299 annual fee, making it the highest annual fee Southwest Airlines credit card. However, it also comes with plenty of perks that can justify it, as I’ll explain below.

There is no cost to add authorized users on the card, so you can add authorized users to your card, and be rewarded for their spending.

The Southwest Performance Business Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a good card to use for purchases abroad.

One of the main reasons you’ll want to consider picking up a card is because of its return on spending, so you’re sure it aligns with what you’re looking for. In the case of the Southwest Performance Business Card, it has a limited number of bonus categories, and spending can also help you toward earning elite status with Rapid Rewards. So let’s cover those details.

The Southwest Performance Business Card offers some potentially useful bonus categories, as follows:

These are some pretty solid bonus categories, though in general, I would only use this card for everyday spending if trying to earn Southwest Airlines status. Based on my valuation of 1.2 cents per point, this is like earning a 4.8% return on the 4x points categories, 2.4% return on the 2x points categories, and a 1.2% return on the 1x points categories.

The Southwest Performance Business Card lets you earn unlimited Tier Qualifying Points (TQPs) toward elite status. Specifically, you can earn 2,500 TQPs toward A-List status for every $5,000 spent on the card.

Southwest A-List status offers perks like priority boarding, a 25% points bonus, same-day standby, priority check-in and security lane access, and a dedicated phone number.

A-List status ordinarily requires earning 35,000 TQPs in a calendar year, so spending on a Southwest Performance Business Card could help you earn that. Whether or not that’s worth it depends on how much you’d otherwise fly with Southwest.

Do note that Southwest recently announced some big changes to its loyalty program, including new status level names and the introduction of a third tier called Platinum. Starting in 2027, A-List status will become Silver status, and earning it will require 35,000 TQPs or 25 qualifying flights.

According to the Southwest Performance Business Card’s terms & conditions, cardholders can earn TQPs on card spending at the current rate of 2,500 TQPs per $5,000 spent through December 31, 2026. After that date, A-List status will become Silver status, and every co-branded Southwest credit card will earn 1 TQP per dollar spent, so $35,000 in spending would get you to Silver.

One of the best values in travel is the Southwest Airlines Companion Pass. For those of you not familiar with Southwest’s Companion Pass, it allows someone else to travel with you for the entire year anywhere Southwest flies.

You still have to pay the taxes on their ticket, but the Companion Pass is valid on both award and revenue tickets. You can change your designated companion three times in a year, so you can potentially even use this for different people.

Historically, you’ve been able to get the Companion Pass by earning 135,000 Rapid Rewards points in a calendar year — and Southwest credit card welcome bonuses counted toward this, along with referral bonuses, anniversary points, bonus points from spending on the card, and more. Starting January 1, 2027, this will no longer be the case.

Southwest is updating its elite status program to have three tiers, the highest of which is called Platinum and gets you unlimited Companion Pass trips. At that time, credit card welcome bonuses and all the other points earning mentioned above will no longer count toward qualifying for the Companion Pass (or any level of status).

To earn Platinum, and therefore the Companion Pass, you’ll instead need to earn 140,000 TQPs or take 100 qualifying flights. This change isn’t specific to the Southwest Performance Business Card, as it applies to welcome bonuses across all Southwest credit cards. But the good news is that welcome bonuses earned before the end of 2026 do count toward Companion Pass qualification, so now is your last chance to take advantage before this opportunity is closed.

I have an entire post on how to redeem Southwest Rapid Rewards points for maximum value, but I’ll briefly cover how redemptions work and how to get the most value out of your points here.

Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, which means that the value you’ll get from your points is tied to the cash cost of Southwest tickets. That said, there are a few different levels, ranging from Basic tickets to Choice Extra fares, with Basic awards usually offering the highest redemption value.

In my experience, the best-value Southwest point redemptions are usually for international routes to destinations like Costa Rica and Aruba. Southwest also flies to Hawaii, which can be a good use of points, but I’ve found that the redemption value is often a bit lower on these in-demand routes. And of course, if you have the Companion Pass your points become twice as valuable because a friend can travel for free minus taxes and fees.

There are no change or cancellation fees on Southwest award bookings, and rebooking a fare when the price drops gets you a refund equal to any difference in points. Just note that Basic fares can only be changed by upgrading to a higher fare bundle, so for a cheaper Basic award you’d want to cancel and rebook rather than change your existing itinerary.

While the Southwest Performance Business Card has a great bonus, the main reason you want to get this card is because of the perks that it offers. For those who fly Southwest with any frequency, the perks should more than cover the annual fee. In fact, for those who are frequent Southwest flyers, this card is almost too good to be true.

Just for having the Southwest Performance Business Card, you’ll receive 9,000 Rapid Rewards points on your account anniversary every year. As I said above, Southwest points can be redeemed for ~1.2 cents each toward airfare, so that’s the equivalent of ~$108 toward airfare annually.

The Southwest Performance Business Card offers a free first checked bag for you and up to eight additional passengers on your same reservation. If you usually check bags on Southwest — especially if you don’t have Southwest status, which gets you a free first checked bag — this benefit alone can quickly help you recoup the annual fee.

For non-elite Southwest travelers, a checked bag costs $45 one-way. If you maxed this benefit out with eight other travelers on a round-trip itinerary with checked bags, you’d be looking at over $800 in value.

When you book a Southwest flight as a Performance Business cardholder, you can select a Preferred or Standard seat at the time of booking, if they’re available. This benefit also extends to eight travelers on your same reservation.

The cost for a Preferred seat can vary from $28 to nearly $50 depending on the flight, so this benefit can also save you some real money.

The Southwest Performance Business Card also offers unlimited upgrades to extra legroom seats for cardholders and up to eight travelers on the same reservation. These upgrades are space available and will start within 48 hours of departure. This is another nice elite-style benefit that can noticeably improve your travel experience on Southwest.

Southwest Performance Business cardholders can board with Group 5, or earlier if they have status or a fare that entitles them to a higher boarding group. Once again, this perk extends to eight additional travelers on the same reservation.

The Southwest Performance Business offers 25% savings on inflight purchases of Wi-Fi and drinks. To take advantage of this, simply pay with your card. You’ll automatically receive a statement credit on eligible inflight purchases.

For having the Southwest Performance Card you receive a credit towards TSA PreCheck, Global Entry, or NEXUS. You can take advantage of this benefit once every four years. (up to $120 as of 10/1/24)

If you are going to use this perk, I’d highly recommend registering for Global Entry over TSA PreCheck. For those of you not familiar, TSA PreCheck gets you expedited US security screening, while Global Entry gets you expedited US immigration clearance.

Why register for Global Entry and not PreCheck? Because Global Entry also comes with TSA PreCheck, while the inverse isn’t true (signing up for TSA PreCheck doesn’t get you Global Entry).

If you have a small business and fly Southwest with any frequency, then the Southwest Performance Business Card is a no brainer. To start, the card has an excellent welcome bonus that could get you a lot of travel, and could even help you earn Companion Pass — at least until the end of 2026, which is coming up very fast.

On an ongoing basis, the card is worth it as well. It has a $299 annual fee but offers 9,000 points per year (which I value at ~$108) and more. This card should pay for itself for anyone who flies Southwest often.

In addition to the Southwest Performance Business Card, Southwest also has the Southwest® Rapid Rewards® Premier Business Credit Card (learn more). How does that card compare? Here’s a quick look:

If you fly Southwest only a handful of times a year, you might prefer this card and its lower annual fee to the more premium Southwest Performance Business.

In addition to comparing the Southwest Performance Business with other Southwest business credit cards, I want to take a minute to recommend another points strategy if you occasionally book award flights on Southwest.

Chase Ultimate Rewards is a transfer partner with Southwest Rapid Rewards, and points transfer at a 1:1 ratio. This means that you could earn points at a faster rate through Ultimate Rewards than through Rapid Rewards, and your points will be more flexible (since you can also transfer them to other airlines and hotel programs).

So, should you earn Rapid Rewards points directly with a Southwest Airlines credit card, or with a Chase Ultimate Rewards credit card?

For context, some of the best cards for earning Chase Ultimate Rewards points include the following:

The Ink Business Preferred Card could be an especially strong pick, considering you’re reading a review of a business credit card — and it has a significantly lower annual fee than the Southwest Performance Business Card.

On top of that, the following four no annual fee cards earn points that can be converted into Ultimate Rewards points at a 1:1 ratio in conjunction with one of the above cards:

The Southwest Performance Business Card is an exceptional option for those who frequently fly Southwest and want the best-possible experience with the airline.

In addition to the solid bonus, the card also offers 9,000 anniversary bonus points, space available Preferred and extra legroom seats, and more. The value of that should add up quickly if you fly Southwest frequently. This is especially true now that Southwest charges fees for checked bags and charges for assigned seats.

#6263. US Army Black Hawk Helicopter Nearly Struck By Fireworks During Dramatic NFL Flyover

A US Army Black Hawk helicopter narrowly avoided a potentially dangerous encounter with stadium fireworks during a pregame flyover at an NFL game between the Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears on November 2, 2026. The incident occurred at Lumen Field in Seattle, Washington, when pyrotechnics erupted while the final helicopter in a four-aircraft formation was still passing over the stadium. Dramatic footage captured the fireworks exploding remarkably close to the military aircraft, prompting audible gasps from spectators.

The flyover was part of the national anthem ceremony ahead of the Monday Night Football matchup, which attracted approximately 70,000 spectators. Although military helicopter appearances are a familiar feature of major sporting events in the United States, the incident raised questions about coordination between stadium personnel and military flight crews. Fortunately, the helicopter continued flying after the fireworks erupted, with no apparent damage reported.

Four US Army Sikorsky UH-60M Black Hawk helicopters from the 2-158th Assault Helicopter Battalion, part of the 16th Combat Aviation Brigade, performed the ceremonial flyover at Lumen Field. The aircraft approached the stadium in formation as part of the pregame celebrations before the Seahawks faced the Chicago Bears. According to MyNorthwest, the first three helicopters passed over the stadium before the fireworks display began. However, the fourth aircraft was still nearby when the stadium's pyrotechnics were activated.

Video footage shared widely on social media shows fireworks launching from the stadium structure and exploding extremely close to the trailing helicopter. From certain camera angles, the pyrotechnics appear to pass alongside the aircraft's rear section, creating the impression that the helicopter might have been struck. The aircraft nevertheless continued its flight behind the other three helicopters, with no visible signs of damage.

The incident was also reported by the New York Post, which highlighted the frightening proximity of the fireworks and the reactions from spectators. While some footage appears to show fireworks passing directly alongside the aircraft, it remains unclear whether any projectile actually made contact. Neither an official explanation for the timing nor confirmation of an aircraft inspection was available in the initial reporting.

Fireworks are generally not compatible with aircraft operating in close proximity, especially during low-altitude helicopter demonstrations. Although a military helicopter such as the UH-60M is designed for demanding operating environments, its rotors, engines, flight controls, and other components remain vulnerable to foreign objects and external damage. A firework exploding near a helicopter could potentially expose its crew to burning debris, heat, and fragments, while also creating a distraction during a maneuver that requires precise aircraft control.

Sikorsky, part of Lockheed Martin, manufactures the Black Hawk, a twin-engine military utility helicopter. Its design emphasizes operational versatility, survivability, and the ability to continue flying under challenging conditions. However, these characteristics should not be mistaken for immunity to airborne hazards. Even a relatively small incident involving a rotor blade or an engine intake could have serious consequences, particularly when an aircraft is operating close to a crowded venue.

A historical example also shows why coordination between aircraft operators and pyrotechnics teams is essential. On July 23, 1982, a Bell UH-1 helicopter crashed in California during the filming of Twilight Zone: The Movie after special-effects explosions detonated too close to the aircraft. The accident killed actor Vic Morrow and two child actors, and injured six other people. According to the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation, debris and heat from the explosions damaged the helicopter's rotor blades, causing the tail rotor assembly to separate and the helicopter to descend uncontrollably. The investigation identified inadequate communication and coordination between the helicopter pilot and film director as contributing factors.

The army has several installations in the DC area.

Despite the potential dangers, aircraft demonstrations and pyrotechnics can be combined in the same organized event when appropriate safety procedures are in place. Airshows regularly combine military aircraft demonstrations, ground-based explosions, smoke effects, and other theatrical elements to recreate combat scenarios or enhance performances, and we have personally witnessed many such impressive performances, including the legendary one at Oshkosh. The key distinction is that these activities require careful planning, clearly defined operating areas, and communication between participating teams. Aircraft must follow predetermined flight paths that keep them away from designated pyrotechnic zones.

The Federal Aviation Administration ( FAA) provides specific guidance for organizing aviation events involving ground-based pyrotechnics. Its airshow safety requirements emphasize documenting pyrotechnic device locations, establishing appropriate public-protection procedures, and coordinating ground operations. The agency also highlights the importance of separating aircraft movements from fireworks displays. Its guidance on mass aircraft demonstrations further stresses the need for detailed flight plans, mandatory briefings, and geographical, vertical, lateral, and time separation between participating aircraft.

For stadium flyovers, timing is everything because helicopters generally fly slower than many fixed-wing aircraft, so they can stay near a venue longer. This makes coordination between flight crews, stadium production teams, and pyrotechnics operators especially important. In Seattle, the fireworks appeared to begin before the final Black Hawk had completely cleared the stadium area. Although the helicopter continued flying without any apparent consequences, the incident demonstrated how a seemingly routine pregame celebration can create an unnecessary aviation hazard.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#6262. Are Marriott Bonvoy Airline Mileage Transfers Worth It? They Could Be, But…

Among hotel loyalty programs, one thing that makes Marriott Bonvoy unique is the ability to (fairly) efficiently convert hotel points into airline miles. While most major hotel loyalty programs allow some sort of opportunity to convert hotel points into airline miles, it typically represents a very bad value.

In this post, I’d like to take a look at the opportunity to convert Marriott points into airline miles. Which airline programs can you move your Marriott points to, what’s the transfer ratio, and is it worth it?

It’s possible to convert Bonvoy points into airline miles, with your choice of nearly 40 different frequent flyer programs. Let’s take a look at which partners Marriott Bonvoy has, what the transfer ratios are, etc.

Marriott points generally convert into airline miles at a 3:1 ratio, and with most partners you get 5,000 bonus miles for every 60,000 Marriott points you transfer.

In other words, 60,000 Bonvoy points will convert into 25,000 airline miles (including the 5,000 bonus miles). You can take advantage of that bonus of 5,000 miles multiple times, meaning that you can convert Bonvoy points into airline miles at a ratio of up to 2.4:1.

Note that you can transfer a minimum of 3,000 Bonvoy points and a maximum of 240,000 Bonvoy points per day. So if you want to transfer more than 240,000 Bonvoy points, you’ll want to do so over multiple days.

Below is a chart with the airline frequent flyer programs you can transfer your Marriott points to, along with the standard transfer ratio, plus the ability to earn a bonus when transferring a minimum of 60,000 points.

While I covered these details above, let me specifically note the exceptions that apply here:

With the major transferable points currencies, converting points into airline miles is typically an instant process. So it’s worth being aware that Marriott points don’t convert into airline miles instantly. Rather, transfers generally take anywhere from a day to a couple of weeks, with transfers for most partners taking anywhere from two to five days.

I’d consider this to be a major weak point of this opportunity. I generally recommend converting points into airline miles in situations where you have a specific use in mind, and that could be a situation where you find award space on a particular flight.

Obviously that’s not exactly useful here, since it could take a couple of weeks for the transfer to happen, and odds are that whatever award availability you were looking at will be gone at that point.

The process of converting Marriott points into airline miles is really straightforward. Just go to the partner transfer page, click the “Transfer Points” button, and then you’ll be asked to enter the information for the account you want to move your points to. There you’ll be able to select how many points you want to transfer, and note that the amounts shown won’t reflect a bonus, if eligible.

It’s important to be sure that the names of the accounts match, as you can only transfer your Marriott points to an airline frequent flyer account that’s also in your name. Also keep in mind that once the miles are in your frequent flyer account, they’ll be subject to the standard airline mileage expiration policies of the program.

While I think converting Marriott points into airline miles could represent a good value, it’s not how I choose to redeem my Bonvoy points.

To briefly crunch some numbers, based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Bonvoy points to be worth 0.7 cents each. At a 2.4:1 transfer ratio (60,000 points per 25,000 miles), that’s like “paying” 1.68 cents per airline mile, which is a pretty decent cost.

Why do I choose not to convert Marriott points into airline miles?

I absolutely don’t think anyone is off base for choosing to convert Marriott points into airline miles. For that matter, this could be a good option if you’re in a crunch, and just need to top off an account for a high value redemption. However, it’s not how I choose to redeem my points, and I don’t think the value is there for most.

It’s more of a last resort redemption option, if you’re truly unable to get value elsewhere. In fairness, that might just be the direction the program is headed. While Bonvoy points have been significantly devalued over the years for hotel redemptions, the mileage conversion options have remained mostly consistent.

While the ability to convert Marriott points into airline miles has been around for a long time, we’re increasingly seeing two-way transfers, where you can convert airline miles into Marriott points.

The idea behind this is great — maybe someone has a lot of airline miles, but really wants to redeem for a hotel stay. Is this a good deal, though? Unfortunately the answer is almost always “no.”

Currently the below programs let you convert airline miles to Marriott Bonvoy, with both the transfer ratios and any exceptions listed.

While I suppose more flexibility is always a good thing, these transfers are almost never worth it. As a reminder, I value Bonvoy points at 0.7 cents each, and you’re getting at most one Bonvoy point per airline mile.

If you have the same valuation I do, at a 1:1 transfer ratio you’re getting up to 0.7 cents per mile, while at a 2:1 transfer ratio, you’re getting up to 0.35 cents per mile. That’s not a rate at which I’d be happy cashing in miles.

It’s possible to convert Marriott points into airline miles with over three dozen programs. While this is the best hotel points to airline miles transfer ratio that you’ll find with any program, it’s still not how I’d choose to redeem my Bonvoy points.

Yes, I appreciate the “insurance” that this redemption option provides, since it essentially creates a floor value for Bonvoy points. However, Bonvoy points are hard to efficiently earn through anything other than hotel stays, so I prefer to save them for hotel stays. I’d rather convert credit card points currencies into airline miles.

Where do you stand on the value of Marriott Bonvoy airline mileage transfers? Have you ever redeemed Bonvoy points this way?

Appreciate this post. Transferred 60,000 Bonvoy points yesterday and today to United. 120K Bonvoy points became 60,000 United miles with their 10,000 bonus on each transfer. They appeared in my account almost instantly. Used my increased UA balance to book an international flight in Polaris, currently pricing at $7000. A far better return on those Bonvoy miles than I ever would have received from any Marriott reservation.

Here in Germany, we don't have that many transferrable point currencies, and also the transfer partners are very limited. I used my Bonvoy points back in the days to transfer them to Korean Air and "rewarded" myself to a First Class award ticket from FRA to ICN for my 50th birthday. Well spent!

ND’s point is the key one IMO. With Bonvoy award pricing all over the place, a lot of redemptions now come in well under 0.7 cents, so the miles route isn’t the last resort it used to be. United at 60K for 30K with that extra bonus is the standout. Randy’s instant datapoint is a nice surprise vs the usual 2 to 5 days. FWIW the flip side of keeping points for hotels is checking what cash would cost first. Google Hotels gives a quick baseline. The same Marriott can price diff depending on which country you search from as inventory and rates vary by market. A free tool like Arbitrica checks it from roughly 195 countries and finds the lowest price in the world. If that cash rate is low, moving the points to miles starts to look smart

Generally I agree with this article. The points can be used with Marriott for better value but if you need to just top off for an airline redemption it may be worth doing. Buying Marriott points could be of good value when there is a 50% or 75% bonus offer.

If one looks at Bonvoy point redemption for award stays these days, unfortunately the average appears well below $.007 USD, maybe somewhere between $.004-$.006. Bonvoy-> Airline Transfers are increasingly becoming a more competitive redemption option. Not all FFPs are created equal, just like not all previously referenced Bonvoy transfer partners are equal. There are some good opportunities. Actually, Bonvoy points transferring to the airline FFP of my choice(s) are now my preferred way to use my Bonvoy points.

#6261. 17 Trips You Should Book a Year in Advance

I'm a firm believer that holidays need a balance of organization and freedom, so that you can enjoy all the long-awaited activities without feeling like they're obligations. Starting to organize and book excursions well in advance can make your experience considerably better, especially when planning trips to particularly popular destinations. Though, that's not the only reason why you should already be thinking about what to add to your 2027 travel bucket list.

Planning a trip a year in advance, long before your suitcase ever leaves the closet, offers up a very particular and potent type of dopamine hit. The moment you confirm a flight or secure a coveted reservation delivers its own quiet thrill, a reminder that the joy of travel lives not only in the trip itself, but in the anticipation that precedes it.

With 2027 shaping up to be a year of more personal, experience-led travel, there's even more reason to start planning ahead. According to Booking.com's 2027 travel predictions, 77 percent of travelers are interested in taking a holiday that pushes them beyond their comfort zone, while 81 percent would choose a destination based on how they want to feel rather than simply where they want to go.

Booking early has myriad practical advantages, too. It can protect you from soaring prices, guarantee access to peak-season experiences, and ensure a plethora of accommodation options that often fill up months before departure. The extra planning room also allows you to seek out lesser-known routes and time your visit to seasonal spectacles. Plus, it offers the underrated delight of months filled with small frissons of excitement every time you think about what is to come. Whether you’re dreaming of spotting wildlife in East Africa or weaving through the Peloponnese in Greece, here's your guide to planning a trip a year in advance for 2027.

This gallery has been updated since its original publish date.

England’s landscapes offer a surprising breadth of adventure for such a compact country, from the rugged drama of the Lake District to the chalk cliffs and wildflower-strewn downs of the South East and the mellow, biscuit-hued villages that string all of this together. A rich tapestry of moors that feel wonderfully remote, market towns that hum with independent food producers, and stretches of coastline where seals bob with the rhythm of the waves can all be woven together, with the added ease of just being able to ring up and book. Outdoorsy types can opt for hiking along windswept coastal paths in Cornwall, paddleboarding through still-water estuaries in Devon, or following ancient woodland trails in the New Forest, while those who prefer a slower pace can settle into long lunches at quaint English vineyards (Chapel Down in Kent and Rathfinny in Sussex, to name a few), wander through sculpture parks or spend languid afternoons in honey-stone villages where the loudest sound is often the church bell.

For those seeking the same sense of escape on a gentler scale, a clutch of estates across England is quietly rethinking the country house stay. Just outside London, The Grove in Hertfordshire is a firm family favorite, amid rolling parkland and its own championship golf course. The addition of two quaint cottages tucked into the grounds in 2025 offers a more private way to experience the estate, with access to its extensive grounds and family-friendly activities, from mini Land Rover rides to archery and woodland walks. Further north, The Tawny in Staffordshire offers a more immersive relationship with the landscape, where architecturally considered treehouses and lakeside retreats complement woodland gardens, dining at The Plumicorn restaurant, and paths to explore across its two adjoining estates. While in Hampshire, Avington Park Estate leans into its historic setting, pairing grand riverside scenery with elegant accommodation and access to fishing, wild swimming, and a range of wellness experiences, including a lakeside sauna pod.

All this, though, with the caveat that some of the most sought-after Great British stays can fill up well ahead of peak weekends and school holidays, so it's worth getting your reservation in early if you have your heart set on a particular property or date in 2027.

The Peloponnese invites a slower, deeper kind of Greek escape, one built around winding coastal roads, mountain passes scented with wild herbs, and ancient sites that appear almost without warning. This southern peninsula feels far removed from the island throngs, yet it offers a richness that rivals any Aegean hotspot. Planning ahead is key, particularly if you want to secure small guesthouses, family-run inns, or farm stays in popular coastal areas during July and August. For a 2027 trip, consider traveling in May, June, or September, when temperatures are generally more comfortable for sightseeing and the roads are less crowded than at the height of summer.

A favorite among avid road trippers, routes here weave through layers of history and landscape. One moment you’re exploring the fortified town of Monemvasia, built on a towering rocky islet connected to the mainland by a narrow causeway, and the next you are wandering through the ruins of Mycenae or the venerable theater at Epidaurus. The distances are manageable with a well-planned itinerary, which leaves ample time to pause at quiet coves, watch fishermen haul in their morning catch, or break for lunch under vine-covered pergolas in medieval villages. Allow at least a week if you want to explore several parts of the peninsula rather than rushing between archaeological sites, and consider choosing a handful of bases, such as Nafplio, Monemvasia, the Mani peninsula, or Pylos, to make the most of the journey.

The Mani peninsula is stark and dramatic, dotted with stone towers and rugged beaches that glow at sunset. To the west, the region opens into long ribbons of sand, olive groves that stretch toward the horizon, and wetlands alive with birdlife. Near Pylos, the Gialova Lagoon is an important stopping point for migratory birds, while the nearby crescent-shaped Voidokilia Beach makes a particularly tempting stop on a coastal drive. Inland, the mountains of Arcadia offer cool respite in summer and timeless hiking trails that trace the contours of rivers and valleys. If you're traveling in 2027, book your preferred accommodation early for peak summer dates, but leave enough room in the itinerary for spontaneous detours. In fact, for travelers drawn to the romance of the open road, there are few places as rewarding or as effortlessly cinematic as the Peloponnese.

For couples planning a celebration trip, Hawaii remains one of the most evocative places to unwind together. The archipelago pairs volcanic drama with serene beaches, vibrant reefs, and an open spirit, while its deeply held sense of community gives romance a grounded, almost effortless quality.

For a romantic escape, the choice of island is just as important as the hotel. On Big Island, volcanic landscapes and stretches of coastline set the scene for a slower-paced holiday, while Oahu combines beautiful beaches with Honolulu's lively restaurants and nightlife. The hotel scene offers plenty of tempting options, from the traditional-style, thatched-roof hale at Rosewood Kona Village and the extensively renovated Mauna Lani, Auberge Collection, to smaller gems such as White Sands Hotel and Surfjack in Waikiki.

For a honeymoon or anniversary trip, it's worth booking your preferred resort and flights in advance, particularly if you're traveling over Christmas, New Year, or during the summer holidays. And if you're hoping to explore more than one island, allow enough time for the additional flights rather than trying to squeeze too much into one trip.

The landscapes of Utah are full of sandstone spires, rust-red cliffs that glow in the late-afternoon light, and labyrinthine slot canyons that twist into shadow and sun. Geology becomes a storybook, particularly at Utahraptor State Park, home to one of the most significant dinosaur bone sites in North America. Located around 15 miles northwest of Moab, the park protects the Dalton Wells Dinosaur Quarry, where thousands of dinosaur bones have been discovered, including those of its namesake predator. Further south, the astonishing petroglyph panels at Newspaper Rock offer a rare glimpse into centuries of Indigenous history, with carvings attributed to Basketmaker, Ancestral Puebloan, and Ute peoples. The rock surface is carved with scenes that feel as vivid today as when they were first etched.

Both sites can be reached from Moab, a small desert hub that continues to evolve. From April to early November 2027, Canyon Spirit, formerly Rocky Mountaineer's Rockies to the Red Rocks service, is scheduled to operate its two-day train journey between Denver and Moab, with an overnight stay in Glenwood Springs. With panoramic windows framing Colorado's mountains, river valleys, and dramatic red-rock canyons, it is a journey that turns the simple act of moving from one place to another into an experience in its own right. Winter, too, brings a different kind of spectacle to Utah, when canyon walls catch the low light and snowfall softens the edges of its famously rugged terrain. For a 2027 trip, it's worth securing your preferred train departure and accommodation in Moab well ahead, particularly if you're traveling in spring or autumn, when temperatures are generally more comfortable for exploring the desert on foot.

Vancouver Island offers a rare kind of quiet that settles over old-growth forests, wild shorelines, and mountain lakes so still they resemble polished stone. It is also a place where Indigenous presence remains central. The lands of the Kwakwaka’wakw, Nuu-chah-nulth, and Coast Salish peoples continue to shape the island’s identity, and planning ahead allows travelers to seek out experiences rooted in cultural respect rather than commercial interpretation. Ferries can fill up quickly during summer, making advance bookings worthwhile on reservable routes and giving you time to curate a thoughtful route. BC Ferries generally opens reservations six months ahead and recommends booking at least four to six weeks before long weekends, so it's worth planning your crossings early if you're traveling with a car or camper van.

On the water, you can join marine excursions informed by generations of coastal knowledge or explore the Salish Sea with Indigenous guides who share their knowledge of the region's history, wildlife, and cultural traditions. Fishing trips with Indigenous-owned outfitters offer another way to experience the island's coastal traditions, while storytelling walks and wildlife encounters reveal how land, sea, and culture are intertwined. Vancouver Island’s landscapes match this richness. Orcas pulse through cold channels, black bears forage along shorelines and in forest clearings, and mist drifts between cedar trees that have stood for centuries. Whether you pitch a tent north of Campbell River or take a slow-rolling road trip in a camper van, this is a destination where the outside world becomes the centerpiece. Summer is a particularly rewarding time to explore, with longer days for hiking and kayaking, while whale-watching opportunities vary by location and season. If you're planning a 2027 escape, check campsite reservation opening dates and arrange popular guided wildlife excursions and Indigenous-led experiences ahead of your visit, particularly for July and August.

Your kids might learn about the rainforest at school—but there’s nothing like seeing it in real life to nurture their interest in nature and inspire their curiosity. Costa Rica is one of the most biodiverse countries in the world, with more than a quarter of its territory protected for conservation, and it’s not just children who are enchanted by bright butterflies, noisy green macaws, bead-eyed tree frogs, and sloths. It’s a relatively small country, so it’s possible to take in the rainforest canopy, pineapple plantations, sandy beaches, and mist-topped mountains all in one trip. From spotting wildlife on guided rainforest walks to exploring hanging bridges around Arenal or watching the waves roll in along the Pacific coast, there are plenty of ways to turn a family holiday into an adventure.

The best eco-lodges, home rentals, and hotels in Costa Rica are worth booking well ahead, particularly for Christmas, Easter, and school holidays. The Pacific coast's dry season generally runs from December to March, with April marking the transition towards the rainy season, making these months popular for beach holidays and outdoor adventures. The Caribbean coast follows a different rainfall pattern, with September and October often among its driest months. Plan in advance and book into one of the country's famous eco-friendly stays—we like the Victorian-style bungalows at Aguas Claras in Puerto Viejo or the luxurious Lapa Rios Lodge on the Osa Peninsula. Aguas Claras welcomes children aged three and over and can arrange activities such as surfing lessons and wildlife excursions, while Lapa Rios, which accepts children aged six and over, offers guided rainforest experiences and opportunities to learn about conservation. For a private stay, there are some truly fantastic Airbnbs in Costa Rica, including treehouses surrounded by tropical greenery and villas near the beaches of Santa Teresa.

For a 2027 family trip, it's worth planning your route as carefully as your accommodation. Winding mountain roads and travel times between regions can make an ambitious itinerary tiring, particularly with younger children. Choose a few bases rather than trying to see everything, and book popular guided activities ahead of time. Some national parks also require advance online tickets, so check the relevant booking arrangements before visiting.

Where to stay: Best Hotels in Costa Rica; Best Rentals in Costa Rica

Though Seoul is famous for its café culture and culinary scene, the kitchens in South Korea's southern regions are drawing travelers down and out of the capital, with tour operators designing itineraries that guide guests through the ingredients, culture, and history of each recipe. Responsible Travel has put together an eight-day experience with departures available throughout much of 2027, inviting travelers to experience regional specialities, spend a night at a Buddhist temple near Gyeongju, explore traditional food markets, and learn to make kimchi. On the coast, Jeollanam-do spotlights fresher, lighter flavors straight from the ocean such as ganjang gejang (soy-marinated crab), plus richer dishes like beef-rib soup. You can also stay in a temple at Baekyangsa, where Buddhist nun and chef Jeong Kwan (of Chef’s Table fame) has a meditative approach to Korean cooking. The temple offers a separate overnight experience featuring a demonstration of her temple cuisine, with sessions generally held monthly and dates released around a month in advance.

Most arriving by air will travel through Seoul at some point—so factor in a few days to check out chefs such as Jungsik Yim and Mingoo Kang, who have been putting the city on the Michelin-starred map with their internationally-acclaimed menus. Kang's restaurant Mingles holds three Michelin stars in the 2026 guide, while Yim's Jungsik has two, making both tempting additions to a food-focused itinerary. For an authentic stay, book into a hanok in Seoul, perhaps in the historic Bukchon neighborhood, where traditional tiled-roof houses sit alongside galleries, tea rooms, and small boutiques. Be aware that tourist sightseeing is restricted between 5 p.m. and 10 a.m. in designated residential streets, so check the local rules before visiting.

Ask most people what’s on their travel bucket list, and you can guarantee that a trip on Belmond's Venice Simplon-Orient-Express is up there. Long associated with romance and timeless glamour, there are few things as enjoyable as a journey on one of these famous trains through Europe. Thanks to a focus on slow travel, you can now justify your ticket as a greener way of getting around. From the moment you arrive at the station and the lacquered dark blue carriages come into view, you feel like you’ve stepped into the pages of an Agatha Christie novel.

There are 70 routes to explore, including Paris to Verona and Amsterdam to Venice. On the Florence to Paris route, squeeze in a stay at Castello di Casole beforehand so you can start your trip with freshly cooked pizza from the hotel’s 16th-century pizza oven and glasses of wine from their vineyard while watching the sun set behind the rolling Tuscan hills.

Once on board and directed to your cabin, there’s little to do but sit back, sip Champagne, and watch as the train station melts away and towns and fields speed past you. A three-course lunch in one of the three 1920s dining cars is next, followed by an afternoon drinking cocktails in 3674, the train’s Art Deco bar car, before dressing in your finery for the evening.

Time slips away as quickly as the snow-capped mountains whizzing past the window, and after a decadent dinner followed by martinis in the bar car—accompanied by the tinkling of a piano and, if you’re lucky, a sing-song from the bar staff—it’s time to climb into bed and let the movement of the train (and aforementioned martinis) lull you to sleep.

If you don’t quite manage the 6 a.m. wake up to see the sunrise over Champagne, then you’ll stir as the train pulls into Paris and coffee and pastries arrive promptly at your cabin. All that’s left is to wonder how quickly you can save for your next Venice Simplon-Orient-Express adventure. With 2027 journeys already available to book, it's worth reserving early if you have a particular route, date, or cabin category in mind.

Uruguay’s summer runs from December to February, although warm weather and beach holidays can extend into March, so it’s a popular winter break for sun-starved travelers (and when seasonal restaurants and hotels are most likely to be open). While Montevideo offers a mix of city beaches, markets, and culture, further along the coast, José Ignacio—a former fishing village turned bustling beach town—draws a fashionable crowd of locals and foreigners. The area has become a magnet for art lovers, foodies, and design enthusiasts, with places such as Posada Ayana, home to James Turrell’s Skyspace installation, and Luz, a wine lodge surrounded by vineyards and olive groves, around ten minutes' drive from José Ignacio. Guests at Posada Ayana can experience Turrell's Ta Khut installation at sunrise and sunset, while Luz offers wine tastings and culinary experiences that make it worth venturing away from the beach.

Seafront favorite Playa Vik continues to attract visitors with its striking architecture, art-filled interiors, and views over Playa Mansa. Just out of town, the high-design Sacromonte Landscape Hotel offers a more secluded escape in the wild sierras of Maldonado, where contemporary cabins overlook the surrounding vineyards and countryside. Although Francis Mallmann’s restaurants Chiringuito and Bodega Garzón are on many bucket lists, few know that visitors can also stay at Casa Anna, the chef's charming guesthouse in nearby Pueblo Garzón. Alongside regular accommodation, Casa Anna offers separately arranged hosted culinary experiences with Mallmann, including shared meals and opportunities to discover his distinctive approach to open-fire cooking.

If you're planning to spend the last of your annual leave in the South American sunshine, aim for late December to experience José Ignacio at its buzziest, but be prepared for higher prices and limited availability at the most sought-after hotels. February and March can offer a quieter alternative, although some seasonal businesses begin winding down as summer draws to a close. For the festive period, booking in advance is particularly worthwhile, especially if you're hoping to secure one of the area's smaller, design-led retreats.

The ski-in-ski-out Park Hyatt Niseko Hanazono boasts Molière Montagne, a restaurant from three-Michelin-starred chef Hiroshi Nakamichi, an impressive selection of restaurants and bars, and hot-spring bathing facilities for unwinding after a day on the slopes. Sansui Niseko offers a fully serviced alternative to townhouses by Kasara or Airbnb (the latter of which are particularly high quality here), with direct ski access to Grand Hirafu's Family Course, an onsen, and spacious suites for those traveling with family or friends.

The outskirts of Sapporo are stunning in the fall, with koyo (the appearance of autumn leaves) at its most colorful around mid-October, but winter is when Niseko really comes into its own. The 2026 to 2027 ski season is scheduled to begin on November 28, with some ski areas planning to remain open into early May, depending on snowfall. January and February are generally the best months for the famously light, dry powder that draws skiers and snowboarders from around the world, although snow conditions can never be guaranteed.

For a trip during the winter season, booking accommodation, ski lessons, and equipment rentals well in advance is a good idea, particularly over Christmas and New Year's Eve. With four interconnected ski areas, a thriving restaurant scene, and plenty of opportunities to warm up in an onsen after a day in the snow, Niseko is the kind of destination where a little advance planning can make all the difference.

Another blockbuster backdrop, Jordan’s archaeological city of Petra was named one of the new seven wonders of the world in 2007 for its extraordinary rock-carved architecture and the Al Siq canyon. A couple of hours' drive from Petra, the sliver of Red Sea coast around Aqaba draws visitors for its sun, souks, and scuba-diving opportunities, with colorful coral reefs and warm waters making it a favorite among underwater explorers. Beyond the coast, the extraordinary landscapes of Wadi Rum are another reason to add Jordan to your 2027 travel wish list. Here, towering sandstone formations and vast desert valleys provide the setting for guided excursions with local Bedouin communities and nights spent beneath the stars at desert camps.

Spring and autumn are among the best times to visit, with milder temperatures making it easier to explore Petra's archaeological treasures and venture into the desert. If you fly into the capital, Amman, a metropolis of ancient tradition and entrepreneurial spirit greets you, alongside a slew of social enterprises such as SEP, a fashion and lifestyle brand working with Palestinian refugee embroiderers, and Beit Sitti, a cooking school founded by three sisters where visitors can learn to prepare traditional Arabic dishes alongside local women.

For those hoping to combine Petra, Wadi Rum, and the Red Sea in one trip, planning ahead allows time to arrange local guides, accommodation, and transport between the country's most spectacular destinations. It's also worth looking into the Jordan Pass, which includes admission to more than 40 attractions, including Petra, and a tourist visa fee waiver for eligible visitors who purchase it before arrival and meet the relevant stay requirements. With travel schedules and regional conditions subject to change, check the latest official advisories before confirming your 2027 plans.

Antarctic travel is still trying to strike a balance between overtourism and sustainable travel, with the International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators recording more than 113,000 tourists traveling to the region during the 2025 to 2026 season. Once accessible only to wealthy explorers or well-funded scientists, it’s exciting that this stark, striking landscape is now attracting a growing number of adventurous travelers, although its increasing popularity raises important questions about protecting one of the world's most fragile environments. Many choose to visit during the austral summer (November to March), when there’s less sea ice and more sun (ideal for kayaking, wildlife watching and, on certain specialist expeditions, skiing and snowshoeing).

From vast penguin colonies and seals resting on ice floes to humpback whales feeding in the Southern Ocean, Antarctica offers extraordinary opportunities for wildlife encounters, both on land and at sea. For many travelers, a polar cruise is one of the most rewarding ways to experience the continent, with expedition vessels offering guided shore landings and Zodiac excursions, while larger ships may provide scenic cruising without disembarkation. Choosing an operator committed to responsible tourism is essential, although even carefully managed expeditions have an environmental footprint. Consider a vessel with hybrid-electric propulsion, such as Ponant’s Le Commandant Charcot, the first hybrid-electric polar exploration ship powered by liquified natural gas, which also carries two onboard scientific laboratories. Or, book with an operator such as Abercrombie & Kent or White Desert, which offers a different way to experience the continent through its fly-in expeditions and luxury land-based camps, including Whichaway Camp.

With the Antarctic travel season concentrated into just a few months and places on specialist expeditions limited, planning a year ahead is particularly worthwhile. Travelers hoping to visit during the popular summer months of December and January (or to secure a place on a small-group expedition) should start comparing itineraries and booking well before departure.

Trekking in the Himalayas comes with its own set of logistical, financial, and physical challenges, so booking well in advance can make a huge difference. Big groups will struggle with spontaneity, and allowing yourself several months to train and prepare for long days on the mountains is well worth the effort. But physical preparation is only part of the equation: Ladakh's high altitude means visitors also need to allow sufficient time to acclimate, particularly when arriving in Leh, which sits at around 11,500 feet above sea level. Local tourism authorities recommend at least 48 hours of rest before heading to higher-altitude areas.

If you’re determined to spot the region’s elusive snow leopard too, a good local guide is essential, and they book up fast. Hemis National Park is one of the world's best-known places to search for these big cats, with experienced trackers scanning the rocky slopes and valleys for signs of movement. Unlike conventional trekking holidays, snow leopard expeditions are best undertaken during the colder months, generally between November and April, when specialist wildlife tours operate in the region. The conditions can be challenging, with freezing temperatures and unpredictable mountain weather, but the rewards can be extraordinary. Ladakh is at its loveliest, and busiest, during the warmer months, from June to September, for those interested in exploring its Buddhist monasteries.

Consider booking through Voygr Expeditions, andBeyond, or Responsible Travel, all of which offer specialist snow leopard expeditions with experienced local guides or trackers. Some itineraries also incorporate visits to local communities and conservation initiatives, including andBeyond's support for the Snow Leopard Conservancy. With several 2027 departures already sold out, securing a place six to 12 months ahead is advisable, especially for those hoping to travel during the peak winter months.

For decades, safari trips centered around Big Five game, but Rwanda has something that Kenya, Zambia, and Botswana do not: silverback mountain gorillas. As a country, Rwanda has been a champion of ecotourism since long before the term went mainstream, with reforestation, conservation, and caps on visitor numbers protecting the environment and the wildlife within it. These efforts have contributed to a remarkable conservation success story, with the mountain gorilla population across the Virunga Massif, which spans Rwanda, Uganda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, increasing from 480 in 2010 to 604 in 2016. In the Virunga Mountains, only eight people may trek to visit a particular gorilla group each day, with encounters limited to one hour. Visitors are told to stay at least 23 feet away to protect the gorillas from human diseases, although the animals themselves may occasionally approach more closely (recall David Attenborough’s encounter in 1978, when he commented, ‘There is more meaning and mutual understanding in exchanging a glance with a gorilla than any other animal I know’).

A collection of established luxury lodges, such as Magashi Camp, Singita Kwitonda Lodge, One&Only’s Gorilla’s Nest, and Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort have proven themselves to experienced safari-goers. While Magashi offers traditional Big Five game drives in Akagera National Park, Singita Kwitonda and Gorilla's Nest provide luxurious bases for gorilla trekking, and Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort is ideally placed for exploring the rainforest and tracking chimpanzees. For those wanting to venture beyond the forests, Lake Kivu offers a completely different perspective on Rwanda's landscapes. The Kivu Queen uBuranga, which began welcoming guests in December 2023, takes travelers across the lake aboard a luxury floating hotel, with opportunities to explore its islands and discover local communities and traditions.

Gorilla trekking permits currently cost $1,500 per person for most international visitors, and with only eight visitors allowed per habituated gorilla group each day, booking several months in advance is strongly recommended, particularly during the drier seasons from June to September and December to February. Those hoping to combine gorilla trekking with a stay at one of the country's most exclusive lodges should start planning even earlier, especially if traveling during peak holiday periods.
